note.saw: Nothing yet: this is the first full render, built straight from a plan for a big sunfish facing left with a doorway in its side.
note.changing: First build: an upright sunfish whose round body holds a tunnel of hexagon cells full of eyes and almond-eyed beings, falling toward a white-gold light, with eye-filled petals and paisleys ringed behind it and the name on a tilted banner.
note.why: The sunfish is already the strangest round fish in the sea, so turning its body into a doorway felt like the most natural move for a vision piece.
note.idea: A mola mola whose round body is a portal: the side of the sunfish opens into an Alex Grey style tunnel of hexagon cells with light at the end, the rim wrapped in filigree and rainbow contour bands, and the name arced along the bottom.

note.saw: The banner sat off to one side like a tilted box, the lower fin would crash into a centered banner, the head was a flat violet crescent, and the small side fin read as a mouth.
note.changing: Centers the banner at the bottom, tips the whole fish so its nose dips down-left, and gives the head a jewel eye with a curl beneath it, green scrolls and a ring of alien script around the portal. A ring of flames is added too, but it ends up hidden under the fish.
note.why: The fish needed room to breathe and a face worth looking at, and tilting it lets the name sit centered without colliding with a fin.

note.saw: The chunky lettering now read well, but the flames were hidden under the fish, the lower fin slid behind the banner, the fish blended into the petals behind it, and the side fin looked like a big tongue.
note.changing: Turns the fish a little further and tightens the banner, flips the flames so they burst outward, adds a dark moat around the silhouette, fills the head with scales that each hold an eye, curls a spiral under the eye like the Eye of Horus, and shrinks the side fin to a small fan.
note.why: A dark gap around the fish separates it from the busy background, and a head full of watching scales gives the creature a real face.

note.saw: The flames now showed but looked like small, even thorns, the stripes around the outline were heavy and generic, and the background was still a tidy ring of petals.
note.changing: Paints the fins and the frilled tail edge as one hot orange-to-pink block with dark linework, thins the outline stripes, swaps the thorns for rounded rainbow flames, and slips small entity faces and faint light rays into the background.
note.why: A bright warm crescent of fins wrapped around the dark portal is what makes the sunfish shape pop, even at a tiny size.

note.saw: The hot fins finally separated from the background, but the top fin and the tail frill fused into one wedge-shaped sail, the flames looked like jelly beans, and the background was a tidy wallpaper ring.
note.changing: Replaces the flat background pattern with a second hexagon tunnel, every cell an eye, converging on the portal, and stretches the flames into longer, thinner rainbow tongues.
note.why: Tunnel inside a tunnel: the fish now sits at the end of a bigger tunnel that rhymes with the doorway in its body, and no dead dark gaps are left.

note.saw: The new background tunnel worked and the flames read as rainbow feathers, but the top fin still merged into the tail frill as one wedge because both wore the same fire colors.
note.changing: Recolors the scalloped tail frill in cool teal and lime so the top fin stands on its own as a blade.
note.why: A hot blade against a cool frill lets the eye find the real sunfish shape: round body, tall fins, frilled rear, no tail.

note.saw: The sunfish now read at thumbnail size; what remained were details: the side fin did not match the other fins, stray dots scattered along the scalloped edges, and the inside of the banner was flat.
note.changing: Redraws the side fin in the same fire and ink as the big fins, smooths the fine lines along the scallops, and gives the banner a dot texture with gold scroll curls at its forked ends.
note.why: Matching fins make the animal read as one body, and the curls tie the banner into the ornament instead of leaving it a plain slab.

note.saw: Up close the portal was strong, with eyes in every cell and beings melting into the light, but the light at the end of the tunnel was a plain white blob and the whole piece felt like flat neon with no glow.
note.changing: Turns the light into a chrysanthemum of petals, adds a glow to the eye and four-pointed sparkles across the background, and tries a soft gold halo around the portal's rim.
note.why: The light at the end of the tunnel should feel like something you could fall into, and glow and sparkle make the neon feel lit from within.

note.saw: SavesFish said the name was not legible: small, blobby letters, the holes in the a and e closed up, and an orange fade with a 3D shadow muddying it. A small-size reading test agreed.
note.changing: Rebuilds the name in the studio's tested letterforms, much larger, in cream with a magenta edge and a dark outline on a calm dark band, with no fade and no 3D; the fish shrinks and tilts further to make room.
note.why: The name has to read instantly; everything else bends around that.

note.saw: The new letters read cleanly but sat flat on their band, with nothing tying them to the gold and cyan trim of the rest of the piece.
note.changing: Adds a thin gold contour around each letter's dark outline, with a soft dark halo behind the word.
note.why: A fine gold line ties the name into the piece's palette without touching the letter shapes, so it stays just as readable.

note.saw: The second artist takes over the first artist's finished draft: a steeply tilted sunfish whose body opens into a tunnel of eyes, with the name now large and legible below.
note.changing: Nothing yet: the finished draft is rendered again so the second artist can study it at full size, as a badge, small, in the reading test, and up close at the eye and a corner.
note.why: Fresh eyes need an honest look at the starting point before deciding what to keep and what to rebuild.
note.idea: Keep the same fish and the same idea, but rebuild it so it reads at a glance: an upright sunfish with a round disc, two tall blades and a frilled tail edge, a portal with real depth, and a darker, cooler hyperspace behind so the hot fish pops.

note.saw: The new fins had parallel edges and read like one wooden plank running through the body, and the lower blade slid behind the banner.
note.changing: Narrows and shortens both blades, and scales the fish down and raises it so the lower blade ends above the banner.
note.why: The disc has to stay whole with the fins slicing cleanly out of it, and nothing should cross the name.

note.saw: Up close, the background of long dark petals was just a spiky texture with flat bands of color.
note.changing: Replaces it with a jewel tunnel of nested hexagon cells, each holding an eye or a being, converging on the portal, and wraps the fish in a collar of curved petals on a dark aura.
note.why: The fish now sits at the end of a bigger tunnel, a tunnel inside a tunnel.

note.saw: The rim band read as an empty dark ring, the scrolls in the face were random hooks, and the small side fin looked like a seashell.
note.changing: Fills the rim band with a ring of small alien faces trailing flame wisps, starts replacing the hooks in the face with tapered vines, and reshapes the side fin into a striped orange-to-magenta bell with an eye.
note.why: The edge felt sparse, and beings crowned with flame are pure hyperspace; a ring of watchers circling the sun gives the rim something to say.

note.saw: The background of long dark petals was a spiky texture with flat bands at 4x.
note.changing: A jewel hex tunnel of nested cells with eyes, converging on the portal, plus a chrysanthemum collar of curved petals on a dark aura. Tried a paisley-chain rim band.
note.why: The fish now sits at the end of a bigger tunnel. The rim band read as an empty dark ring, so it had to go.

note.saw: Even with its faces, the dark rim band still read as an empty ring at badge size, and the side fin still looked like a seashell.
note.changing: Swaps the rim band for a slim border of alien script between gold lines, sets large jester-hatted 'machine elves' near the rim as watchers, adds jewel roundels at both ends of the banner, cools the petal collar to blues and teals, and redraws the side fin as a slim teal paddle with rays and an eye.
note.why: Beings with flame crowns are pure hyperspace, and the cool ring of petals lets the warm fish jump forward.

note.saw: At 4x the fins were a plain gradient with loose strings, and the whole field averaged to grey haze at badge size.
note.changing: Feather barbs sweeping off a bright spine in the fins, a doubled vortex twist in the portal, dotted rings in every cell, and the lattice recolored as a spiraling rainbow.
note.why: Hyperspace should swirl. Color that follows the tunnel's spiral makes the walls feel like they are turning.

note.saw: The collar was dark and uniform; the clavus strip was a flat teal gradient.
note.changing: A crown of glints on the collar tips, scale texture and eyes in the clavus, a fine neon core line inside the letters (shapes unchanged), hidden lattice rows trimmed.
note.why: Sparkle at the edge of the sun; the name gains a neon-tube shine without losing any clarity.

note.saw: Olive and brown had crept into the rainbow, the fish could separate harder from the field, and the eye needed more presence.
note.changing: Takes olive and brown out of the rainbow, deepens the dark moat behind the collar, adds an orbiting ring of alien script around the sunfish, glowing star glints, a cross-shaped flare on the light at the end of the tunnel, and a first try at flame lashes on the eye.
note.why: Light pouring from inside the belly and a crowned eye give the creature presence, and the deeper moat pulls the fish forward out of the field.

note.saw: Up close, the gaps between the bands of the fish's outline and body were plain, and the collar petals looked flat where they met.
note.changing: Shades the base of every collar petal for depth and runs dotted hairlines through every gap in the outline and body bands.
note.why: Micro dots you only find when you lean in reward close looking, and the shading makes the petals overlap in space.

note.saw: The collar was dark and uniform, and the scalloped tail frill was a flat teal fade.
note.changing: Crowns the collar's petal tips with glints, fills the tail frill with scales and eyes, and threads a fine white neon line inside each letter of the name without changing their shapes.
note.why: Sparkle at the edge of the sun, and the name gains a neon-tube shine without losing any clarity.

note.saw: Round 19 held together: an iconic upright sunfish, a blazing portal, a rainbow vortex behind. But past the petal tips hyperspace was the same dark everywhere, so the field still read a bit like wallpaper.
note.changing: Lights a band of cells just beyond the collar, their cores lifting toward pale lilac and fading with distance (kept dark near the banner), puts tiny glowing portals in the banner's end roundels, lets the cells swell and shrink ring by ring, and adds a flare where the top fin's tip pierces the outer rim.
note.why: Light that falls off with distance turns wallpaper into a room, and the small portals at the ends of the name repeat the piece's heart at a smaller scale, the self-similarity this kind of geometry is made of.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's lit band of cells, tiny portals, breathing cells and rim-piercing flare, and turned down its orbiting heads, rim clipping and stained-glass fin because that rim band and that fin were already gone.

visions.seen: The sunfish swallowed a sun and wears it as a belly. The chrysanthemum is blazing out through its side, and a ring of little green watchers orbits the whole thing like moons that just learned to blink.
suggestions: The pectoral "lantern" at the front of the portal, left of the light (about x 145-165, y 145-170 in the 400 box). Right now it's an opaque orange-to-magenta bell, and it still reads as a seashell or a lipstick. I see it as a stained-glass fan lit from behind by the chrysanthemum: 5 to 7 ribs fanning out from a base near the eye, each cell a see-through jewel (fill-opacity around 0.55, cyan / magenta / gold in turn) with a thin white inner edge, and a soft screen-blend glow on the edge that faces the light. In hyperspace everything is lit from inside. If the portal light shines *through* the fin, the face and the portal become one being instead of two parts stuck together.

The entity heads orbiting in the outer dark band, about 16 alien faces with flame crowns. They all stare straight ahead, evenly spaced, like a row of stickers, and the loose flame wisps drift loose beside them. What if every head leaned about 15 to 20 degrees along the orbit, all the same way, with its pupils slid toward the portal's vanishing point, so they're all *watching the breakthrough*? Then string them on one thin gold orbit thread (about 0.8 px, with a tiny bead between each pair of heads), and curl every wisp clockwise so the whole band turns like a wheel. The elves are never idle wallpaper: they attend, they present, they spin. Keep them stopping at the banner ends, as they do now.

The dorsal blade's tip at top center, where it meets the outer gold ring (about x 228, y 15). Right now it only overlaps the ring. What if that were the moment the fish *pierces the membrane*: cut the ring line for 3 to 4 px on each side of the blade, and put a small 8-ray flare where it breaks through (white core, thin cyan and magenta rays, screen blend, r about 10)? A creature punching out through the mandala's skin is the most DMT gesture the piece has. It's almost there.

The corona petals between 10 and 12 o'clock (top left, about x 115-200, y 20-60) push past the glyph ring into the dark band and crowd the entity heads sitting there. What if the corona were clipped at the inner glyph ring, so each shell keeps its own lane: a corona of fire, then a ring of runes, then the lane where the watchers orbit? Nested shells that never bleed into each other read as *depth*, as layers of hyperspace stacked behind one another, not one big pile.
visions.keep: the upright mola, which you can read at a glance: round disc, tall sickle dorsal and anal blades, the scalloped green clavus. The off-center chrysanthemum light deep in the portal, with entities at three depths. The scale-patterned head with the wheel-iris eye. The cool indigo hex-eye hyperspace behind, which lets the hot fish pop. And the SavesFish nameplate exactly as it is: cream letters, pink edge, thick dark outline, on the calm dark swallowtail band. It reads instantly at 240 px, so nothing goes on or behind those letters.

visions.seen: The watchers inside the portal have turned their teardrop heads toward the light like sunflowers, the pectoral has opened into a ribbed green fan, and the slim rune rim lets the corona breathe. I see all of it. But past the petal tips, hyperspace is the same dark everywhere, as if the sun in its belly isn't allowed out.
suggestions: The ring of hex-eye cells just beyond the corona petal tips, all the way around the fish. That's about r 135 to 175 from the portal light's world center (near x 189, y 162). It shows most at the top right between the dorsal blade and the rim (x 260-345, y 35-110), at the top left (x 70-130, y 25-60) and down the left edge (x 20-60, y 110-240). I see the chrysanthemum's light escaping there, like an eclipse. The dark ink moat right behind the petals stays as it is. Beyond it comes a lit band: each cell's dark core (#120632) lifts toward a pale lilac-white (#E8DEFF at fill-opacity about 0.45 near r 140, fading to 0 by r 175), and the eyes in those cells open brighter, with cream whites and a gold iris. Fade it out above y 295 so the banner keeps its dark surround. Light that falls off with distance turns hyperspace into a *room* instead of wallpaper: near cells lit, far cells in shadow. And the dark-outlined petals become silhouettes against glow, so at badge size the whole creature reads as a burning disc ringed in light.

The two jewel roundels at the banner's ends (about x 75, y 285 and x 325, y 285). Right now they're spiral-web targets, the same as the cells in the field. What if each one held a tiny copy of the portal? Keep the dark ring stack, and inside it put a pinprick chrysanthemum: a white 2 px core, a 12-petal cream-gold rosette about r 6 made from the same `pet` motif, and a soft white-to-gold-to-orange radial glow, set a hair off center the way the big one is. The piece would repeat its own heart at a smaller scale, and that self-similarity, the big portal echoed in the small ones, is the signature of DMT geometry. They sit beyond the ends of the band, so the letters stay untouched. Keep the glow inside r 9 so they frame the word like two lit finials instead of pulling the eye away from it.

The hex-eye lattice itself, from the corona out to the rim. Every ring uses the same cell scale (0.92), so the field is even, and the five thin dashed ripple circles around the light barely show. I see the walls breathing instead. Let cell size swell and shrink in a wave from ring to ring (cellScale about 0.8 + 0.14·sin(j·1.1)), and give each swollen ring a slightly brighter outer band. Then pulses of big bright cells and small dim cells ripple outward from the portal like a heartbeat through the lattice. The rhythm lives in the stuff of the walls, not in hairlines drawn on top. In hyperspace the architecture is alive: it breathes, it pulses, it pushes outward from the source.
visions.keep: The upright mola you can read at a glance: round disc, sickle dorsal and anal blades with their spines of eyes shrinking toward the tips, the scalloped green clavus. The off-center chrysanthemum deep in the portal and the teardrop entities now leaning toward it. They attend, exactly right. The ribbed green pectoral fan with its eye, and the wheel-iris eye on the scaled violet head. The rainbow flames burning hot only around the face while the tail side stays cool. The slim gold rune rim and the cool indigo field. And the SavesFish nameplate exactly as it is: cream letters, magenta edge, gold-and-ink outline on the calm dark swallowtail band. It reads instantly at 240 px, so nothing goes on or behind those letters.

visions.seen: The fish strung itself with stars: an 8-ray flare where the dorsal tip stabs the sky, a lane of runes behind the corona, and hyperspace now runs hot magenta where it touches the fish and cools to teal at the rim. I feel all of it. But a huge white cross has slammed down over the heart, and when I stare into the flower I see a camera glint where the chrysanthemum should be spinning.
suggestions: The light at the end of the tunnel, about x 181, y 155. In #116 there were four rings of chrysanthemum petals there. Now the cross flare (star4 at scale 26, plus the 45° one at scale 12) lies over them like a sheet of white glass, and at badge size the heart reads as a sparkle emoji. What if the flare shrank to about scale 8 at opacity 0.6, dropping the 45° one, and the chrysanthemum climbed to the top of the stack, drawn after the flare with mix-blend screen? Give it Fibonacci rings: 8, 13, 21, 34 petals from the core outward, with the `pet` mirrored (scale(-sc, sc)) on every other ring so the rings curl against each other. Run the strokes white to gold to hot magenta to violet going outward, so the flower burns down into the tunnel's blue. Keep the white core r 3 and the soft bloom, so the badge still has its blinding point. Then echo it in the wheel-iris eye (about x 120, y 137): swap its 4-point catchlight for a tiny 6-petal rosette. The jeweled chrysanthemum is the first thing hyperspace shows you, and it never glints; it unfolds and spins, ring against ring. A 4-point star is a camera's word for light. A counter-curling rosette is hyperspace's word, and an eye that reflects it shows the fish has seen inside itself.

The mouth, the little gold-and-magenta ring at the front of the face (about x 95, y 164). The fish watches but never speaks. I see it speaking in visible language: a thin ribbon pouring from the lips, out over the rainbow flame curl in front of it, then coiling into the violet field at the left. It could be an ink band tapering from 6 px to 1.5 px with gold hairline edges, carrying the same cream glyphs as the rune rings, shrinking along the curl. It ends in a 1.5-turn spiral (r about 9, centered near x 36, y 150, inside the field between the rim and the corona lane), and the last glyphs break off as 3 or 4 tiny floating jewels: a cube, a pyramid, a bead, each with a faint cyan glow. The elves don't talk, they sing objects into the air. Language you can *see* is one of the purest DMT signs, and it turns the fish from a vessel into an entity. It stays far above the banner (y < 200), so the name is untouched.

The outer edge of the hex-eye field, just inside the gold rim (about r 146 to 186 from the badge center 200, 200), all the way round. Right now the cells reach the rim at full size and the ring chops them in half like a cookie cutter. What if the lattice fell into a Circle Limit there instead? For each cell at badge radius ρ > 146, move its center to ρ' = 146 + 40·tanh((ρ − 146)/40) and scale it by sech²((ρ − 146)/40). The last rings shrink to a third and smaller, more rings crowd in, and no cell ever touches the rim. (Keep the unmapped lattice, clipped outside r 200, for the square's corners.) Then the edge of the badge becomes the edge of infinity, a dome you are looking up into, where the walls never stop and only get smaller. The log-polar tunnel already shrinks toward the portal; shrinking toward the rim too gives hyperspace two poles, which is exactly how it folds.
visions.keep: The upright mola, now wrapped in its white dotted contour, with flare-tipped blades and the scalloped green clavus. The new dark rune lane behind the corona (each shell in its own lane, yes). The magenta-near, teal-far warmth in the field. The teardrop watchers leaning into the light, the ribbed pectoral fan, the scaled violet head with the wheel-iris eye, and the rainbow flames hot only around the face. And the SavesFish nameplate exactly as it is: cream letters, magenta edge, gold-and-ink outline on the calm dark swallowtail band. It reads instantly at 240 px, so nothing goes on or behind those letters.

visions.seen: The little portals at the ends of the banner have caught fire. Two tiny suns flank the name like lit lanterns, and the heart has learned to echo itself. But the sunfish is still only the doorway. It hasn't fallen in yet, and the long petals of its crown all hold one shape, as if hyperspace forgot it never stops changing.
suggestions: Inside the portal tunnel, on the spiral from the lower-right wall in toward the light (from about x 206, y 182 to x 189, y 164 in the 400 box). I see the fish falling into its own heart: three tiny copies of the mola silhouette (the dors + anal + clav + body union, through `<use>`), about 13, 8 and 5 px tall (scale about 0.037, 0.023, 0.014). Each one is turned so its head points at the light, curving along the tunnel's 0.8 twist. Fill them cream #FFF6C0 with a 0.6 px ink edge (vector-effect non-scaling-stroke), a gold pinprick eye, and a faint cyan glow. Keep them outside r 9 of the light, and slot them between the three rings of watchers so no face gets covered. A fish that holds a portal that holds the fish is the Droste fold, recursion with no bottom. The roundels echo the portal; this echoes the creature itself. When you lean in, the badge swallows its own tail.

The cream spine running up the dorsal blade (from about x 229, y 113 to the tip at x 247, y 21) and down the anal blade (about x 229, y 211 to x 247, y 300). I see twin serpents coiling up that spine. Two strands, cyan and magenta (0.9 px over a 2 px ink underlay), swing to either side of the blade's midline at an amplitude of about 0.28 × the blade's width there, so they taper toward the tip. Set their phase so they cross exactly at each eye of the spine (t = 0.12, 0.3, 0.46, 0.6, 0.72, 0.82, 0.9), so the eyes become the knots of the helix. Add thin gold rungs (0.4 px) between the strands at each quarter turn, and let the cream spine thin to a hairline axis. The double helix, the cosmic serpent coiled around a column of eyes, is the oldest vision of the code that writes life. It turns the blades from fins into living nerves that carry the light up and down.

The outer ring of long collar petals (petA, 30 of them, tips about r 140 from the light). They show between 11 o'clock and 5 o'clock: top right between the dorsal blade and the rim (x 250-330, y 20-110), and down the right side behind the clavus (x 290-345, y 120-260). I see them changing as they turn. Make four versions of petA that differ only in the last fifth of the petal, and choose by angle along that visible arc. Round tips at 11 o'clock become forked serpent tongues by 1 o'clock, then hooked jester-hat tips each with a gold bell bead by 3 o'clock, then faceted crystal shards with one white facet line by 5 o'clock. The hidden left side behind the flames stays round. Keep the light crown on every tip. In hyperspace nothing holds its form: things transform while you watch. A ring that metamorphoses as it goes round freezes that change in one frame, and it brings back the jester elves without crowding the rim again.
visions.keep: The glowing mini-portal roundels at both ends of the banner (Vision 2, taken, and they work) and the flare where the dorsal tip pierces the rim. The upright mola you can read at a glance, with its rainbow echo bands, flare-tipped blades, scalloped clavus and violet scaled head with the wheel-iris eye. The watchers leaning into the light, the magenta-near, teal-far field, the slim rune lane. Vision 3's plea about the white cross over the heart still stands. And the SavesFish nameplate exactly as it is: cream letters, magenta edge, gold-and-ink outline on the calm dark swallowtail band. It reads instantly at 240 px, so nothing goes on or behind those letters.
